notes: Original cases for Kiln wire v0 (Frozen). Bytes were produced by spec/reference/kiln_ref.py and frozen here. Names kelp are original. This is not the benchmark message type. gld-kiln is the only library.

cases.title: Bool false is the byte 0
cases.paragraph: A bool is one byte. 0 is false and 1 is true.

cases.title: Bool true is the byte 1
cases.paragraph: A bool is one byte. 0 is false and 1 is true.

cases.title: Any bool byte other than 0 or 1 is a type error
cases.paragraph: Any byte other than 0 or 1 is a type error.

cases.title: Int8 uses two's complement
cases.paragraph: An i8 is one byte, two's complement.

cases.title: Int16 is little-endian
cases.paragraph: An i16 is two bytes, little-endian.

cases.title: Int32 is little-endian
cases.paragraph: An i32 is four bytes, little-endian.
cases.notes: The bytes are 04 03 02 01. A big-endian read would not yield 16909060.

cases.title: A short i32 is an end-of-buffer error
cases.paragraph: A length that extends past the buffer is an end-of-buffer error.

cases.title: Int64 is eight little-endian bytes
cases.paragraph: An i64 is eight bytes, little-endian.

cases.title: UInt8 is one byte
cases.paragraph: A u8 is one byte.

cases.title: UInt16 is little-endian
cases.paragraph: A u16 is two bytes, little-endian.

cases.title: Float32 keeps the IEEE-754 bits
cases.paragraph: An f32 is four bytes, IEEE-754 little-endian.

cases.title: Float64 keeps the IEEE-754 bits
cases.paragraph: An f64 is eight bytes, IEEE-754 little-endian. The bit pattern is preserved.

cases.title: Float64 preserves negative zero
cases.paragraph: The bit pattern is preserved, including negative zero.

cases.title: Float64 preserves a NaN payload
cases.paragraph: The bit pattern is preserved, including a NaN payload.

cases.title: An empty string is a zero length and no bytes
cases.paragraph: A string is a u32 byte length, then UTF-8 bytes. There is no terminator.

cases.title: A string is a length prefix plus UTF-8 bytes
cases.paragraph: A string is a u32 byte length, then UTF-8 bytes. There is no terminator.

cases.title: A string may contain multi-byte UTF-8
cases.paragraph: A string is a u32 byte length, then UTF-8 bytes.

cases.title: A string with an invalid UTF-8 byte is rejected
cases.paragraph: decode checks bounds and UTF-8.

cases.title: A string length that runs past the buffer is rejected
cases.paragraph: A length that extends past the buffer is an end-of-buffer error, and the decoder does not allocate from that length.

cases.title: A string longer than 16 MiB is a limit error
cases.paragraph: A string or a byte run longer than 16 MiB is a limit error.
cases.notes: The body is absent. The length alone is over the limit, so the decoder must not allocate that many bytes.

cases.title: A byte string is a length prefix plus raw bytes
cases.paragraph: List of u8 and a byte blob have the same layout: a u32 count, then that many bytes.

cases.title: An empty list is a zero count
cases.paragraph: A list is a u32 count, then the elements.

cases.title: A list of i32 is a count and then the elements
cases.paragraph: A list is a u32 count, then the elements. A list of a fixed-width number is little-endian.

cases.title: A list of u8 is a count and then raw bytes
cases.paragraph: List of u8 is a u32 count, then that many bytes.

cases.title: A list count that runs past the buffer is rejected
cases.paragraph: A length that extends past the buffer is an end-of-buffer error, and the decoder does not allocate from that length.

cases.title: A list count greater than 16777216 is a limit error
cases.paragraph: A list count greater than 16,777,216 is a limit error.
cases.notes: No elements follow the count. The decoder must reject the count before allocating.

cases.title: Optional absence is the byte 0
cases.paragraph: An optional is one byte, 0 or 1. A 0 is absence and is not followed by a value.

cases.title: Optional presence is the byte 1 and then the value
cases.paragraph: A 1 is followed by the inner value.

cases.title: An optional tag other than 0 or 1 is a type error
cases.paragraph: An optional is one byte, 0 or 1.

cases.title: A struct is its fields in declaration order with no padding
cases.paragraph: There is no padding between fields. A struct is the concatenation of its fields in declaration order.

cases.title: A dict is a count and then key/value pairs
cases.paragraph: A dict is a u32 count, then key/value pairs. Keys are strings.
cases.notes: The wire order is b then a. The reader returns both pairs. The writer sorts keys so two encodes of the same map match.

cases.title: Sixty-four nested lists are within the depth limit
cases.paragraph: Nesting deeper than 64 containers is a depth error. Sixty-four containers are still valid.

cases.title: Sixty-five nested lists are a depth error
cases.paragraph: Nesting deeper than 64 containers is a depth error.

cases.title: Bytes after the value are rejected
cases.paragraph: decode requires the buffer to contain exactly one value.

cases.title: An empty buffer is not a value
cases.paragraph: decode requires the buffer to contain exactly one value.

cases.title: A frame is KLN0, Frozen profile 0, and the schema hash
cases.paragraph: encode_framed writes 16 bytes and then one Frozen value. The magic is KLN0, the profile is Frozen (0), and the schema hash follows.

cases.title: A frame with the wrong magic is rejected
cases.paragraph: decode_framed rejects a wrong magic.

cases.title: A frame whose profile is not Frozen is rejected
cases.paragraph: decode_framed rejects a profile other than Frozen.

cases.title: A frame whose schema hash does not match the destination is rejected
cases.paragraph: decode_framed rejects a hash that does not match the destination type.

cases.title: A short frame header is rejected
cases.paragraph: A frame is 16 bytes and then one Frozen value. A shorter buffer is not a frame.

cases.title: A tensor is KLNT, dtype Float64, and raw little-endian values
cases.paragraph: write_f64 writes a 64-byte header and then raw little-endian Float64 values. The magic is KLNT and dtype 1 means Float64. The payload starts at offset 64.

cases.title: A tensor may contain zero elements
cases.paragraph: The element count is a little-endian integer at offset 8. A count of zero has a header and no payload.

cases.title: A tensor with the wrong magic is rejected
cases.paragraph: The tensor magic is the ASCII bytes KLNT.

cases.title: A tensor dtype other than Float64 is rejected
cases.paragraph: Dtype 1 means Float64.

cases.title: A tensor whose payload is shorter than the count is rejected
cases.paragraph: The payload is count times eight bytes, starting at offset 64. A shorter buffer is not a complete tensor.
